name: SEROTONIN(5HT) RANDOM URINE
interpretation:
Note
This test measures the amount of serotonin in the blood. Serotonin is a chemical derived from the amino acid tryptophan. It is produced as needed by the nervous system, mainly the brain, but also by special cells in the bronchial tubes (lungs) and gastrointes nal tract. More than 90% of serotonin in the blood is found in the platelets. Serotonin helps transmit nerve impulses and constrict blood vessels, is a par cipant in the wake‐sleep cycle, and affects mood. Serotonin is metabolized by the liver and its metabolites, primarily 5‐HIAA (5‐hydroxyindoleace c acid, a muscle s mulant), are excreted in the urine.Normally, serotonin is present in small varying quan es in the blood. Large quan es of serotonin and 5‐HIAA may be produced con nuously or intermi ently by some carcinoid tumors. In order to diagnose the condi on, serotonin level followed by 24 hours 5‐HIAA test and tumor itself must be located and biopsiedA significantly increased level of serotonin in a person with carcinoid syndrome symptoms is sugges ve but not diagnos c of a carcinoid tumor.


Interpretation:
Someone with symptoms may still have a carcinoid tumor even if the concentrations of serotonin and 5-HIAA are normal.The affected person may have a tumor that does not secrete serotonin or one that secretes it intermi ently. A person with no symptoms and normal or low levels of serotonin and 5‐HIAA is unlikely to have a serotonin‐secre ng carcinoid
tumor.
There are a variety of drugs that can affect the serotonin test, including morphine, monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors such as reserpine, methyldopa, and lithium.Extremely high levels of serotonin can cause a condi on known as serotonin syndrome, with toxic and poten ally fatal effects.
